208	class DecisionHistory:
209	    """A JSON-file-backed store of decision records.
210	
211	    The file is UTF-8 compact JSON (a single trailing newline) holding only a
212	    ``records`` array sorted by ``(id, at)`` in Unicode code point order.
213	    """
214	
215	    def __init__(self, path: str) -> None:
216	        if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
217	            raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
218	        self._path = path
219	        self._records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
220	        if os.path.exists(path):
221	            self._records = self._load()
222	        else:
223	            self._persist()
224	
225	    def _load(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
226	        with open(self._path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
227	            try:
228	                raw = json.load(handle)
229	            except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
230	                raise ValueError(f"{self._path!r} does not contain valid JSON") from exc
231	        if not isinstance(raw, dict) or set(raw) != {"records"}:
232	            raise ValueError(f"{self._path!r} must contain only a records array")
233	        records = raw["records"]
234	        if not isinstance(records, list):
235	            raise ValueError(f"{self._path!r}: records must be an array")
236	        return [_validate_entry(entry, index) for index, entry in enumerate(records)]
237	
238	    def _persist(self) -> None:
239	        data = _dump(self._records)
240	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self._path))
241	        fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=".decision-history-")
242	        try:
243	            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
244	                handle.write(data)
245	                handle.flush()
246	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
247	            os.replace(tmp, self._path)
248	        except OSError:
249	            try:
250	                os.unlink(tmp)
251	            except OSError:
252	                pass
253	            raise
254	
255	    def record(
256	        self,
257	        record_id: str,
258	        at: str,
259	        facts: dict[str, bool],
260	        rules: list[dict[str, Any]],
261	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
262	        """Evaluate ``rules`` and persist the outcome under ``(record_id, at)``."""
263	        _check_non_empty_str(record_id, "record_id")
264	        matched = _matched_rules(at, facts, rules)
265	        if any(entry["id"] == record_id and entry["at"] == at for entry in self._records):
266	            raise ValueError(f"duplicate record for (record_id, at): ({record_id!r}, {at!r})")
267	        if matched:
268	            decision: str | None = matched[0]["result"]
269	            trace = [f"{rule['id']}@{rule['ver']}" for rule in matched]
270	            basis: dict[str, Any] | None = _snapshot_basis(matched[0])
271	        else:
272	            decision = None
273	            trace = []
274	            basis = None
275	        entry = {"id": record_id, "at": at, "decision": decision, "trace": trace, "basis": basis}
276	        self._records.append(entry)
277	        try:
278	            self._persist()
279	        except OSError:
280	            self._records.remove(entry)
281	            raise
282	        return copy.deepcopy(entry)
283	
284	    def replay(self, record_id: str, at: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
285	        """Return a copy of the most recent record for ``record_id`` at or before ``at``."""
286	        _check_non_empty_str(record_id, "record_id")
287	        _check_time(at, "at")
288	        best: dict[str, Any] | None = None
289	        for entry in self._records:
290	            if entry["id"] == record_id and entry["at"] <= at:
291	                if best is None or entry["at"] > best["at"]:
292	                    best = entry
293	        if best is None:
294	            raise KeyError(record_id)
295	        return copy.deepcopy(best)
296	
297	    def evolution(self, record_id: str, start: str, end: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
298	        """Return stored snapshots for ``record_id`` within the closed ``[start, end]``.
299	
300	        Only already-persisted records are read; nothing is recomputed, written,
301	        or otherwise mutated. ``record_id`` must be a non-empty string and
302	        ``start``/``end`` valid UTC seconds with ``start <= end``; otherwise
303	        ``ValueError`` is raised. Matching records are returned in ascending
304	        ``at`` order; when none match, ``KeyError`` is raised. The result is a
305	        deep copy with keys ``id, start, end, entries``; each entry has keys
306	        ``at, decision, trace, basis, changes``, where ``changes`` lists, in
307	        the order ``decision, trace, basis``, the fields differing from the
308	        previous entry (the first entry's ``changes`` is ``[]``).
309	        """
310	        _check_non_empty_str(record_id, "record_id")
311	        _check_time(start, "start")
312	        _check_time(end, "end")
313	        if start > end:
314	            raise ValueError(f"start must not be after end: {start!r} > {end!r}")
315	        matched = [
316	            entry
317	            for entry in self._records
318	            if entry["id"] == record_id and start <= entry["at"] <= end
319	        ]
320	        if not matched:
321	            raise KeyError(record_id)
322	        matched.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["at"])
323	        entries: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
324	        previous: dict[str, Any] | None = None
325	        for entry in matched:
326	            if previous is None:
327	                changes: list[str] = []
328	            else:
329	                changes = [
330	                    field
331	                    for field in _EVOLUTION_FIELDS
332	                    if entry[field] != previous[field]
333	                ]
334	            entries.append(
335	                {
336	                    "at": entry["at"],
337	                    "decision": copy.deepcopy(entry["decision"]),
338	                    "trace": copy.deepcopy(entry["trace"]),
339	                    "basis": copy.deepcopy(entry["basis"]),
340	                    "changes": changes,
341	                }
342	            )
343	            previous = entry
344	        return {"id": record_id, "start": start, "end": end, "entries": entries}
345	
346	    def audit(self, record_id: str, start: str, end: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
347	        """Return a hash-chained audit trail for ``record_id`` over ``[start, end]``.
348	
349	        Only already-persisted records are read; nothing is recomputed, written,
350	        or otherwise mutated. ``record_id`` must be a non-empty string and
351	        ``start``/``end`` valid UTC seconds with ``start <= end``; otherwise
352	        ``ValueError`` is raised. Matching records are returned in ascending
353	        ``at`` order; when none match, ``KeyError`` is raised. The result is a
354	        deep copy with keys ``id, start, end, root, entries``; each entry has
355	        keys ``at, decision, trace, basis, previous, digest``, the first four
356	        following the record contract.
357	
358	        Let ``C`` be the UTF-8 compact JSON bytes (non-ASCII unescaped, no
359	        trailing newline) of the current entry restricted to
360	        ``at, decision, trace, basis`` in that key order. The first entry's
361	        ``previous`` is 64 ASCII ``0`` characters; every later entry's
362	        ``previous`` is the preceding entry's ``digest``. ``digest`` is the
363	        lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of ``previous``'s ASCII bytes immediately
364	        followed by ``C``; ``root`` is the last entry's ``digest``.
365	        """
366	        _check_non_empty_str(record_id, "record_id")
367	        _check_time(start, "start")
368	        _check_time(end, "end")
369	        if start > end:
370	            raise ValueError(f"start must not be after end: {start!r} > {end!r}")
371	        matched = [
372	            entry
373	            for entry in self._records
374	            if entry["id"] == record_id and start <= entry["at"] <= end
375	        ]
376	        if not matched:
377	            raise KeyError(record_id)
378	        matched.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["at"])
379	        entries: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
380	        previous = _AUDIT_GENESIS
381	        for entry in matched:
382	            digest = _audit_digest(previous, entry)
383	            entries.append(
384	                {
385	                    "at": entry["at"],
386	                    "decision": copy.deepcopy(entry["decision"]),
387	                    "trace": copy.deepcopy(entry["trace"]),
388	                    "basis": copy.deepcopy(entry["basis"]),
389	                    "previous": previous,
390	                    "digest": digest,
391	                }
392	            )
393	            previous = digest
394	        return {
395	            "id": record_id,
396	            "start": start,
397	            "end": end,
398	            "root": previous,
399	            "entries": entries,
400	        }
401	
402	    def audit_bundle(self, record_ids: Any, start: str, end: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
403	        """Return one hash-chained bundle of audit reports over ``[start, end]``.
404	
405	        Only already-persisted records are read; nothing is recomputed,
406	        written, or otherwise mutated. ``record_ids`` must be a non-empty list
407	        of unique non-empty strings and ``start``/``end`` valid UTC seconds
408	        with ``start <= end``; otherwise ``ValueError`` is raised and the
409	        inputs are left untouched. Each id is audited once in ascending
410	        Unicode code point order; if any id has no record in the closed
411	        interval, ``KeyError`` is raised and no partial result is returned.
412	
413	        The result is a deep copy with keys ``start, end, root, reports``;
414	        ``reports`` holds each id's complete audit result in that same order,
415	        preserving the per-report contract. Let ``h0`` be 64 ASCII ``0``
416	        characters and ``Pi`` the UTF-8 compact JSON bytes (non-ASCII
417	        unescaped, no trailing newline) of the i-th report restricted to
418	        ``id, root`` in that key order. ``hi`` is the lowercase hexadecimal
419	        SHA-256 of ``h{i-1}``'s ASCII bytes immediately followed by ``Pi``;
420	        the bundle ``root`` is ``hn``.
421	        """
422	        if not isinstance(record_ids, list) or not record_ids:
423	            raise ValueError("record_ids must be a non-empty list of record id strings")
424	        seen: set[str] = set()
425	        for index, record_id in enumerate(record_ids):
426	            _check_non_empty_str(record_id, f"record_ids[{index}]")
427	            if record_id in seen:
428	                raise ValueError(

"""Persistent, replayable history of policy decisions."""

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import hashlib
import json
import os
import tempfile
from typing import Any

from .policy import _check_non_empty_str, _check_time, _matched_rules, _validate_rules

_RECORD_KEYS = ("id", "at", "decision", "trace", "basis")
_BASIS_KEYS = ("id", "ver", "source", "priority", "from", "to", "when", "result")
_EVOLUTION_FIELDS = ("decision", "trace", "basis")
_AUDIT_PAYLOAD_KEYS = ("at", "decision", "trace", "basis")
_AUDIT_ENTRY_KEYS = ("at", "decision", "trace", "basis", "previous", "digest")
_AUDIT_REPORT_KEYS = ("id", "start", "end", "root", "entries")
_AUDIT_EXPECTED_KEYS = ("id", "start", "end", "root")
_AUDIT_GENESIS = "0" * 64
_HEX_DIGITS = frozenset("0123456789abcdef")


def _check_trace_entry(value: Any, field: str) -> str:
    if not isinstance(value, str):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be a string of the form id@ver")
    rule_id, sep, ver = value.rpartition("@")
    if not sep or not rule_id or not ver.isdigit() or int(ver) < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be a string of the form id@ver")
    return value


def _validate_entry(entry: Any, index: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
    field = f"records[{index}]"
    if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != set(_RECORD_KEYS):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{field} must be a dict with exactly the keys id, at, decision, trace, basis"
        )
    _check_non_empty_str(entry["id"], f"{field}.id")
    _check_time(entry["at"], f"{field}.at")
    decision = entry["decision"]
    if decision is not None and not isinstance(decision, str):
        raise ValueError(f"{field}.decision must be a string or null")
    trace = entry["trace"]
    if not isinstance(trace, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{field}.trace must be a list of id@ver strings")
    for position, item in enumerate(trace):
        _check_trace_entry(item, f"{field}.trace[{position}]")
    basis = entry["basis"]
    if basis is not None:
        try:
            _validate_rules([basis])
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"{field}.basis is not a valid rule: {exc}") from exc
        # Normalize the snapshot to the canonical key order in memory so every
        # history method returns the same basis shape; the file is not rewritten.
        entry["basis"] = _snapshot_basis(basis)
    return entry


def _snapshot_basis(rule: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    when = rule["when"]
    if when is not None:
        when = {key: when[key] for key in sorted(when)}
    return {
        "id": rule["id"],
        "ver": rule["ver"],
        "source": rule["source"],
        "priority": rule["priority"],
        "from": rule["from"],
        "to": rule["to"],
        "when": when,
        "result": rule["result"],
    }


def _dump(records: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> bytes:
    ordered = sorted(records, key=lambda entry: (entry["id"], entry["at"]))
    text = json.dumps({"records": ordered}, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
    return (text + "\n").encode("utf-8")


def _audit_digest(previous: str, entry: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    payload = {key: entry[key] for key in _AUDIT_PAYLOAD_KEYS}
    content = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
    return hashlib.sha256(previous.encode("ascii") + content.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def _check_hex64(value: Any, field: str) -> str:
    if (
        not isinstance(value, str)
        or len(value) != 64
        or any(char not in _HEX_DIGITS for char in value)
    ):
        raise ValueError(f"{field} must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters")
    return value


def _check_time_window(start: Any, end: Any, field: str) -> None:
    _check_time(start, f"{field}.start")
    _check_time(end, f"{field}.end")
    if start > end:
        raise ValueError(f"{field}.start must not be after {field}.end")


def _validate_audit_entry(entry: Any, index: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Validate one audit entry and return a normalized deep copy of it."""
    field = f"entries[{index}]"
    if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != set(_AUDIT_ENTRY_KEYS):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{field} must be a dict with exactly the keys "
            "at, decision, trace, basis, previous, digest"
        )
    _check_time(entry["at"], f"{field}.at")
    decision = entry["decision"]
    if decision is not None and not isinstance(decision, str):
        raise ValueError(f"{field}.decision must be a string or null")
    trace = entry["trace"]
    if not isinstance(trace, list):
        raise ValueError(f"{field}.trace must be a list of id@ver strings")
    for position, item in enumerate(trace):
        _check_trace_entry(item, f"{field}.trace[{position}]")
    basis = entry["basis"]
    if basis is not None:
        try:
            _validate_rules([basis])
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise ValueError(f"{field}.basis is not a valid rule: {exc}") from exc
        basis = _snapshot_basis(basis)
    _check_hex64(entry["previous"], f"{field}.previous")
    _check_hex64(entry["digest"], f"{field}.digest")
    return {
        "at": entry["at"],
        "decision": copy.deepcopy(decision),
        "trace": copy.deepcopy(trace),
        "basis": basis,
        "previous": entry["previous"],
        "digest": entry["digest"],
    }


def verify_audit(report: Any, expected: Any) -> bool:
    """Verify an audit report against an expected summary by recomputation.

    ``report`` must be a dict with exactly the keys ``id, start, end, root,
    entries``; ``id`` a non-empty string, ``start``/``end`` valid UTC seconds
    with ``start <= end``, and ``entries`` a non-empty list whose ``at``
    values are strictly increasing and lie in the closed interval
    ``[start, end]``. Each entry must have exactly the keys ``at, decision,
    trace, basis, previous, digest``; the first four follow the audit entry
    contract, and ``previous``/``digest`` must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal
    characters. ``expected`` must have exactly the keys ``id, start, end,
    root`` and is validated the same way. Any violation raises ``ValueError``.

    Returns ``False`` when the shared fields differ between ``report`` and
    ``expected``. Otherwise each entry's ``basis`` (and its ``when`` keys) is
    normalized to the canonical key order and the chain is recomputed exactly
    as :meth:`DecisionHistory.audit` defines it: the first ``previous`` is 64
    ASCII ``0`` characters, every later ``previous`` is the preceding entry's
    ``digest``, and ``digest`` is the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of
    ``previous``'s ASCII bytes immediately followed by ``C``. Any chain,
    digest, or root mismatch returns ``False``; otherwise ``True``.

    The function touches neither history nor files and does not mutate its
    inputs.
    """
    if not isinstance(report, dict) or set(report) != set(_AUDIT_REPORT_KEYS):
        raise ValueError(
            "report must be a dict with exactly the keys id, start, end, root, entries"
        )
    _check_non_empty_str(report["id"], "report.id")
    _check_time_window(report["start"], report["end"], "report")
    _check_hex64(report["root"], "report.root")
    entries = report["entries"]
    if not isinstance(entries, list) or not entries:
        raise ValueError("report.entries must be a non-empty list")
    normalized: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    previous_at: str | None = None
    for index, entry in enumerate(entries):
        normalized.append(_validate_audit_entry(entry, index))
        at = entry["at"]
        if previous_at is not None and at <= previous_at:
            raise ValueError("report.entries must be strictly increasing in at")
        if not report["start"] <= at <= report["end"]:
            raise ValueError(f"entries[{index}].at lies outside [start, end]")
        previous_at = at
    if not isinstance(expected, dict) or set(expected) != set(_AUDIT_EXPECTED_KEYS):
        raise ValueError(
            "expected must be a dict with exactly the keys id, start, end, root"
        )
    _check_non_empty_str(expected["id"], "expected.id")
    _check_time_window(expected["start"], expected["end"], "expected")
    _check_hex64(expected["root"], "expected.root")
    for key in _AUDIT_EXPECTED_KEYS:
        if report[key] != expected[key]:
            return False
    previous = _AUDIT_GENESIS
    for entry in normalized:
        if entry["previous"] != previous:
            return False
        if entry["digest"] != _audit_digest(previous, entry):
            return False
        previous = entry["digest"]
    return report["root"] == previous


class DecisionHistory:
    """A JSON-file-backed store of decision records.

    The file is UTF-8 compact JSON (a single trailing newline) holding only a
    ``records`` array sorted by ``(id, at)`` in Unicode code point order.
    """

    def __init__(self, path: str) -> None:
        if not isinstance(path, str) or not path:
            raise ValueError("path must be a non-empty string")
        self._path = path
        self._records: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        if os.path.exists(path):
            self._records = self._load()
        else:
            self._persist()

    def _load(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        with open(self._path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            try:
                raw = json.load(handle)
            except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
                raise ValueError(f"{self._path!r} does not contain valid JSON") from exc
        if not isinstance(raw, dict) or set(raw) != {"records"}:
            raise ValueError(f"{self._path!r} must contain only a records array")
        records = raw["records"]
        if not isinstance(records, list):
            raise ValueError(f"{self._path!r}: records must be an array")
        return [_validate_entry(entry, index) for index, entry in enumerate(records)]

    def _persist(self) -> None:
        data = _dump(self._records)
        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self._path))
        fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=directory, prefix=".decision-history-")
        try:
            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as handle:
                handle.write(data)
                handle.flush()
                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
            os.replace(tmp, self._path)
        except OSError:
            try:
                os.unlink(tmp)
            except OSError:
                pass
            raise

    def record(
        self,
        record_id: str,
        at: str,
        facts: dict[str, bool],
        rules: list[dict[str, Any]],
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Evaluate ``rules`` and persist the outcome under ``(record_id, at)``."""
        _check_non_empty_str(record_id, "record_id")
        matched = _matched_rules(at, facts, rules)
        if any(entry["id"] == record_id and entry["at"] == at for entry in self._records):
            raise ValueError(f"duplicate record for (record_id, at): ({record_id!r}, {at!r})")
        if matched:
            decision: str | None = matched[0]["result"]
            trace = [f"{rule['id']}@{rule['ver']}" for rule in matched]
            basis: dict[str, Any] | None = _snapshot_basis(matched[0])
        else:
            decision = None
            trace = []
            basis = None
        entry = {"id": record_id, "at": at, "decision": decision, "trace": trace, "basis": basis}
        self._records.append(entry)
        try:
            self._persist()
        except OSError:
            self._records.remove(entry)
            raise
        return copy.deepcopy(entry)

    def replay(self, record_id: str, at: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return a copy of the most recent record for ``record_id`` at or before ``at``."""
        _check_non_empty_str(record_id, "record_id")
        _check_time(at, "at")
        best: dict[str, Any] | None = None
        for entry in self._records:
            if entry["id"] == record_id and entry["at"] <= at:
                if best is None or entry["at"] > best["at"]:
                    best = entry
        if best is None:
            raise KeyError(record_id)
        return copy.deepcopy(best)

    def evolution(self, record_id: str, start: str, end: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return stored snapshots for ``record_id`` within the closed ``[start, end]``.

        Only already-persisted records are read; nothing is recomputed, written,
        or otherwise mutated. ``record_id`` must be a non-empty string and
        ``start``/``end`` valid UTC seconds with ``start <= end``; otherwise
        ``ValueError`` is raised. Matching records are returned in ascending
        ``at`` order; when none match, ``KeyError`` is raised. The result is a
        deep copy with keys ``id, start, end, entries``; each entry has keys
        ``at, decision, trace, basis, changes``, where ``changes`` lists, in
        the order ``decision, trace, basis``, the fields differing from the
        previous entry (the first entry's ``changes`` is ``[]``).
        """
        _check_non_empty_str(record_id, "record_id")
        _check_time(start, "start")
        _check_time(end, "end")
        if start > end:
            raise ValueError(f"start must not be after end: {start!r} > {end!r}")
        matched = [
            entry
            for entry in self._records
            if entry["id"] == record_id and start <= entry["at"] <= end
        ]
        if not matched:
            raise KeyError(record_id)
        matched.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["at"])
        entries: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        previous: dict[str, Any] | None = None
        for entry in matched:
            if previous is None:
                changes: list[str] = []
            else:
                changes = [
                    field
                    for field in _EVOLUTION_FIELDS
                    if entry[field] != previous[field]
                ]
            entries.append(
                {
                    "at": entry["at"],
                    "decision": copy.deepcopy(entry["decision"]),
                    "trace": copy.deepcopy(entry["trace"]),
                    "basis": copy.deepcopy(entry["basis"]),
                    "changes": changes,
                }
            )
            previous = entry
        return {"id": record_id, "start": start, "end": end, "entries": entries}

    def audit(self, record_id: str, start: str, end: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return a hash-chained audit trail for ``record_id`` over ``[start, end]``.

        Only already-persisted records are read; nothing is recomputed, written,
        or otherwise mutated. ``record_id`` must be a non-empty string and
        ``start``/``end`` valid UTC seconds with ``start <= end``; otherwise
        ``ValueError`` is raised. Matching records are returned in ascending
        ``at`` order; when none match, ``KeyError`` is raised. The result is a
        deep copy with keys ``id, start, end, root, entries``; each entry has
        keys ``at, decision, trace, basis, previous, digest``, the first four
        following the record contract.

        Let ``C`` be the UTF-8 compact JSON bytes (non-ASCII unescaped, no
        trailing newline) of the current entry restricted to
        ``at, decision, trace, basis`` in that key order. The first entry's
        ``previous`` is 64 ASCII ``0`` characters; every later entry's
        ``previous`` is the preceding entry's ``digest``. ``digest`` is the
        lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of ``previous``'s ASCII bytes immediately
        followed by ``C``; ``root`` is the last entry's ``digest``.
        """
        _check_non_empty_str(record_id, "record_id")
        _check_time(start, "start")
        _check_time(end, "end")
        if start > end:
            raise ValueError(f"start must not be after end: {start!r} > {end!r}")
        matched = [
            entry
            for entry in self._records
            if entry["id"] == record_id and start <= entry["at"] <= end
        ]
        if not matched:
            raise KeyError(record_id)
        matched.sort(key=lambda entry: entry["at"])
        entries: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
        previous = _AUDIT_GENESIS
        for entry in matched:
            digest = _audit_digest(previous, entry)
            entries.append(
                {
                    "at": entry["at"],
                    "decision": copy.deepcopy(entry["decision"]),
                    "trace": copy.deepcopy(entry["trace"]),
                    "basis": copy.deepcopy(entry["basis"]),
                    "previous": previous,
                    "digest": digest,
                }
            )
            previous = digest
        return {
            "id": record_id,
            "start": start,
            "end": end,
            "root": previous,
            "entries": entries,
        }

    def audit_bundle(self, record_ids: Any, start: str, end: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Return one hash-chained bundle of audit reports over ``[start, end]``.

        Only already-persisted records are read; nothing is recomputed,
        written, or otherwise mutated. ``record_ids`` must be a non-empty list
        of unique non-empty strings and ``start``/``end`` valid UTC seconds
        with ``start <= end``; otherwise ``ValueError`` is raised and the
        inputs are left untouched. Each id is audited once in ascending
        Unicode code point order; if any id has no record in the closed
        interval, ``KeyError`` is raised and no partial result is returned.

        The result is a deep copy with keys ``start, end, root, reports``;
        ``reports`` holds each id's complete audit result in that same order,
        preserving the per-report contract. Let ``h0`` be 64 ASCII ``0``
        characters and ``Pi`` the UTF-8 compact JSON bytes (non-ASCII
        unescaped, no trailing newline) of the i-th report restricted to
        ``id, root`` in that key order. ``hi`` is the lowercase hexadecimal
        SHA-256 of ``h{i-1}``'s ASCII bytes immediately followed by ``Pi``;
        the bundle ``root`` is ``hn``.
        """
        if not isinstance(record_ids, list) or not record_ids:
            raise ValueError("record_ids must be a non-empty list of record id strings")
        seen: set[str] = set()
        for index, record_id in enumerate(record_ids):
            _check_non_empty_str(record_id, f"record_ids[{index}]")
            if record_id in seen:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"record_ids must not contain duplicates: {record_id!r}"
                )
            seen.add(record_id)
        _check_time(start, "start")
        _check_time(end, "end")
        if start > end:
            raise ValueError(f"start must not be after end: {start!r} > {end!r}")
        reports = [
            self.audit(record_id, start, end)
            for record_id in sorted(record_ids)
        ]
        root = _AUDIT_GENESIS
        for report in reports:
            payload = json.dumps(
                {"id": report["id"], "root": report["root"]},
                ensure_ascii=False,
                separators=(",", ":"),
            )
            root = hashlib.sha256(
                root.encode("ascii") + payload.encode("utf-8")
            ).hexdigest()
        return copy.deepcopy(
            {"start": start, "end": end, "root": root, "reports": reports}
        )

145	def evaluate(
146	    at: str, facts: dict[str, bool], rules: list[dict[str, Any]]

148	    """Evaluate versioned rules against facts at a UTC second timestamp.

151	    ``id@ver`` in ranking order and ``decision`` is the top rule's ``result``

155	    if not matched:
156	        return None, []
157	    trace = [f"{rule['id']}@{rule['ver']}" for rule in matched]

161	def _conditions_compatible(a: dict[str, bool] | None, b: dict[str, bool] | None) -> bool:
162	    """Return whether two ``when`` conditions can hold simultaneously.
163	
164	    ``None`` means unconstrained. Conditions are incompatible only when they
165	    assign opposite booleans to a shared key.
166	    """
167	    if a is None or b is None:
168	        return True
169	    for key, value in a.items():
170	        if key in b and b[key] is not value:
171	            return False
172	    return True

175	def _snapshot_rule(rule: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
176	    """Return a deep-copied rule snapshot with stable key order.
177	
178	    Keys are ordered ``id, ver, source, priority, from, to, when, result``
179	    and ``when`` keys are sorted in Unicode code point order.
180	    """
181	    when = rule["when"]
182	    if when is not None:
183	        when = {key: when[key] for key in sorted(when)}
184	    return {
185	        "id": rule["id"],
186	        "ver": rule["ver"],
187	        "source": rule["source"],
188	        "priority": rule["priority"],
189	        "from": rule["from"],
190	        "to": rule["to"],
191	        "when": when,
192	        "result": rule["result"],
193	    }

196	def _find_conflicts(ranked: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
197	    """List conflicts between ranked rules as ``winner``/``loser`` triples.
198	
199	    For ranked indices ``i < j``, a pair conflicts when the results differ
200	    and the ``when`` conditions can hold simultaneously; the earlier rule is
201	    the winner.
202	    """
203	    conflicts: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
204	    for i in range(len(ranked)):
205	        winner = ranked[i]
206	        for j in range(i + 1, len(ranked)):
207	            loser = ranked[j]
208	            if winner["result"] != loser["result"] and _conditions_compatible(
209	                winner["when"], loser["when"]
210	            ):
211	                conflicts.append(
212	                    {
213	                        "winner": [winner["source"], winner["id"], winner["ver"]],
214	                        "loser": [loser["source"], loser["id"], loser["ver"]],
215	                    }
216	                )
217	    return conflicts

220	def compile_rules(at: str, rules: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
221	    """Compile the rules effective at ``at`` into rules and conflicts.
222	
223	    Reuses the full validation of :func:`evaluate` for ``at`` and ``rules``
224	    (raising ``ValueError`` on anything invalid), keeps rules in their
225	    ``[from, to)`` window, retains only the highest ``ver`` per
226	    ``(source, id)``, and orders the survivors with :func:`evaluate`'s ranking.
227	
228	    ``conflicts`` lists, for ranked indices ``i < j``, pairs whose results
229	    differ and whose ``when`` conditions can hold simultaneously; the earlier
230	    rule is the winner. The returned structure is a deep copy with stable key
231	    order.
232	    """
233	    ranked = _effective_rules(at, rules)
234	    compiled_rules = [_snapshot_rule(rule) for rule in ranked]
235	    conflicts = _find_conflicts(ranked)
236	    return {"at": at, "rules": compiled_rules, "conflicts": conflicts}

239	def policy_attestation(at: str, rules: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
240	    """Attest a :func:`compile_rules` result with a SHA-256 digest.
241	
242	    ``at`` and ``rules`` are validated exactly as in :func:`compile_rules`;
243	    any type, time, rule-field, ``[from, to)`` interval, or duplicate
244	    ``(source, id, ver)`` error raises ``ValueError`` without mutating the
245	    inputs.

247	    Let ``policy`` be the :func:`compile_rules` result and let ``C`` be the
248	    UTF-8 bytes of ``json.dumps(policy, ensure_ascii=False,
249	    separators=(',', ':'))`` (with no trailing newline). Returns a deep copy
250	    with keys ``at``, ``policy``, ``digest``; ``policy`` keeps every
251	    :func:`compile_rules` key order, ordering, ``when`` Unicode code point
252	    sort, and ``conflicts`` order, and ``digest`` is the lowercase 64-char
253	    hex SHA-256 of ``C``. Equal-valued inputs yield byte-identical results.
254	    """
255	    policy = compile_rules(at, rules)
256	    canonical = json.dumps(policy, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
257	    digest = hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
258	    return {"at": at, "policy": copy.deepcopy(policy), "digest": digest}

264	def _conflict_identity(conflict: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, str, int, str, str, int]:
265	    """Return the six-element identity of a conflict: winner then loser."""

269	def policy_delta(
270	    from_at: str, to_at: str, rules: list[dict[str, Any]]
271	) -> dict[str, Any]:
272	    """Diff the :func:`compile_rules` results at two UTC timestamps.
273	
274	    Both timestamps must be valid UTC seconds of the form
275	    ``YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`` with ``from_at <= to_at``; ``rules`` is
276	    validated exactly as in :func:`compile_rules`. Any type, time,
277	    rule-structure, or ordering violation raises ``ValueError`` without
278	    mutating the inputs.
279	
280	    The rules effective at each timestamp are compiled separately and
281	    identified by ``(source, id)``. Returns a deep copy with keys ``from``,
282	    ``to``, ``rules``, ``conflicts``. ``rules`` lists, ordered by ``source``
283	    (``law`` before ``org``) then ``id`` in Unicode code point order, one
284	    entry per rule that was ``added`` (only at ``to_at``), ``removed`` (only
285	    at ``from_at``), or ``updated`` (present at both but with a different
286	    compiled value); identical rules are omitted. Each entry has keys
287	    ``source``, ``id``, ``kind``, ``before``, ``after``; ``before``/``after``
288	    are the corresponding compiled rule snapshots (with :func:`compile_rules`
289	    key order and ``when`` sorting) or ``None``.
290	
291	    ``conflicts`` has keys ``added``, ``removed``. A conflict's identity is
292	    the six-element value of its ``winner`` array followed by its ``loser``
293	    array. ``added`` lists, in the ``to_at`` compile order, the conflicts
294	    present only at ``to_at``; ``removed`` lists, in the ``from_at`` compile
295	    order, those present only at ``from_at``. Each conflict keeps the keys
296	    ``winner``, ``loser`` with deep-copied values. When nothing differs,
297	    ``rules`` is empty and both conflict arrays are empty.
298	    """
299	    _check_time(from_at, "from_at")
300	    _check_time(to_at, "to_at")
301	    if from_at > to_at:
302	        raise ValueError(f"from_at must not be after to_at: {from_at!r} > {to_at!r}")
303	    before_compiled = compile_rules(from_at, rules)
304	    after_compiled = compile_rules(to_at, rules)
305	
306	    before_rules = {
307	        (rule["source"], rule["id"]): rule for rule in before_compiled["rules"]
308	    }
309	    after_rules = {
310	        (rule["source"], rule["id"]): rule for rule in after_compiled["rules"]
311	    }
312	    entries: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
313	    for key in sorted(
314	        set(before_rules) | set(after_rules),
315	        key=lambda item: (_SOURCE_ORDER[item[0]], item[1]),
316	    ):
317	        before = before_rules.get(key)
318	        after = after_rules.get(key)
319	        if before is not None and after is not None and before == after:
320	            continue
321	        if before is None:
322	            kind = "added"
323	        elif after is None:
324	            kind = "removed"
325	        else:
326	            kind = "updated"
327	        entries.append(
328	            {
329	                "source": key[0],
330	                "id": key[1],
331	                "kind": kind,
332	                "before": before,
333	                "after": after,
334	            }
335	        )
336	
337	    before_conflicts = before_compiled["conflicts"]
338	    after_conflicts = after_compiled["conflicts"]
339	    before_identities = {_conflict_identity(c) for c in before_conflicts}
340	    after_identities = {_conflict_identity(c) for c in after_conflicts}
341	    added_conflicts = [
342	        {"winner": list(c["winner"]), "loser": list(c["loser"])}
343	        for c in after_conflicts
344	        if _conflict_identity(c) not in before_identities
345	    ]
346	    removed_conflicts = [
347	        {"winner": list(c["winner"]), "loser": list(c["loser"])}
348	        for c in before_conflicts
349	        if _conflict_identity(c) not in after_identities
350	    ]
351	    return {
352	        "from": from_at,
353	        "to": to_at,
354	        "rules": entries,
355	        "conflicts": {"added": added_conflicts, "removed": removed_conflicts},
356	    }

359	def policy_schedule(
360	    start: str, end: str, rules: list[dict[str, Any]]
361	) -> dict[str, Any]:
362	    """Compile the policy at the rule boundaries inside a time range.
363	
364	    ``start`` and ``end`` must be valid UTC seconds of the form
365	    ``YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`` with ``start <= end``; ``rules`` is validated
366	    exactly as in :func:`compile_rules`. Any type, time, rule-structure, or
367	    ordering violation raises ``ValueError`` without mutating the inputs.
368	
369	    The candidate timestamps are ``start`` plus every rule ``from`` and
370	    non-``None`` ``to`` falling in ``(start, end]``, deduplicated and sorted
371	    ascending; :func:`compile_rules` is called at each candidate. The first
372	    point is always kept; for each later candidate the function computes
373	    :func:`policy_delta` from the previously kept point to the candidate and
374	    keeps the point unless that delta reports no changes at all (``rules``
375	    empty and both ``conflicts`` arrays empty).
376	
377	    Returns a deep copy with keys ``start``, ``end``, ``points``. Each point
378	    has keys ``at``, ``rules``, ``conflicts``, ``delta``; ``rules`` and
379	    ``conflicts`` are exactly the same-named :func:`compile_rules` values at
380	    ``at`` and keep that contract at every level. The first point's ``delta``
381	    is ``None``; a later point's ``delta`` is the full :func:`policy_delta`
382	    result described above.
383	    """
384	    _check_time(start, "start")
385	    _check_time(end, "end")
386	    if start > end:
387	        raise ValueError(f"start must not be after end: {start!r} > {end!r}")
388	    _validate_rules(rules)
389	    first = compile_rules(start, rules)
390	    candidates = {start}
391	    for rule in rules:
392	        for boundary in (rule["from"], rule["to"]):
393	            if boundary is not None and start < boundary <= end:
394	                candidates.add(boundary)
395	    points = [
396	        {
397	            "at": first["at"],
398	            "rules": first["rules"],
399	            "conflicts": first["conflicts"],
400	            "delta": None,
401	        }
402	    ]
403	    previous_at = start
404	    for at in sorted(candidates - {start}):
405	        compiled = compile_rules(at, rules)
406	        delta = policy_delta(previous_at, at, rules)
407	        if (
408	            not delta["rules"]
409	            and not delta["conflicts"]["added"]
410	            and not delta["conflicts"]["removed"]
411	        ):
412	            continue
413	        points.append(
414	            {
415	                "at": compiled["at"],
416	                "rules": compiled["rules"],
417	                "conflicts": compiled["conflicts"],
418	                "delta": delta,
419	            }
420	        )
421	        previous_at = at
422	    return {"start": start, "end": end, "points": points}
423

425	def policy_schedule_attestation(
426	    start: str, end: str, rules: list[dict[str, Any]]
427	) -> dict[str, Any]:
428	    """Attest a :func:`policy_schedule` result with a SHA-256 hash chain.
429	
430	    ``start``, ``end``, and ``rules`` are validated exactly as in
431	    :func:`policy_schedule`; any invalid value raises ``ValueError`` without
432	    mutating the inputs.
433	
434	    Let ``S`` be the :func:`policy_schedule` result. Returns a deep copy with
435	    top-level keys ``start``, ``end``, ``root``, ``points``; ``start`` and
436	    ``end`` come from ``S`` and ``points`` keeps ``S``'s point order. Each
437	    point has keys ``at``, ``rules``, ``conflicts``, ``delta``, ``previous``,
438	    ``digest``; the first four equal the corresponding ``S`` point at every
439	    level and keep its key order. The first point's ``previous`` is 64 ASCII
440	    ``0`` characters; every later point's ``previous`` is the previous
441	    point's ``digest``.
442	
443	    Let ``C`` be the UTF-8 bytes (with no newline) of
444	    ``json.dumps`` applied to the current point restricted to the keys
445	    ``at``, ``rules``, ``conflicts``, ``delta`` in that order, with
446	    ``ensure_ascii=False`` and ``separators=(',', ':')``. ``digest`` is the
447	    lowercase 64-char hex SHA-256 of the ASCII bytes of ``previous`` followed
448	    immediately by ``C``; ``root`` is the last point's ``digest``.
449	    Equal-valued inputs yield byte-identical results.
450	    """
451	    schedule = policy_schedule(start, end, rules)
452	    points: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
453	    previous = "0" * 64
454	    digest = previous
455	    for point in schedule["points"]:
456	        content = {
457	            "at": point["at"],
458	            "rules": copy.deepcopy(point["rules"]),
459	            "conflicts": copy.deepcopy(point["conflicts"]),
460	            "delta": copy.deepcopy(point["delta"]),
461	        }
462	        canonical = json.dumps(content, ensure_ascii=False, separators=(",", ":"))
463	        digest = hashlib.sha256(
464	            previous.encode("ascii") + canonical.encode("utf-8")
465	        ).hexdigest()
466	        attested = dict(content)
467	        attested["previous"] = previous
468	        attested["digest"] = digest
469	        points.append(attested)
470	        previous = digest
471	    return {
472	        "start": schedule["start"],
473	        "end": schedule["end"],
474	        "root": digest,
475	        "points": points,
476	    }
